_comment: Feed registry. Every entry must carry its licence and the attribution string that licence requires. EU Delegated Regulation 2017/1926 Art. 8(3) separately requires we display the source AND the last-update time of static data, regardless of licence — so `attribution` is not optional even for public-domain feeds. Feeds are fetched from their publishers directly, never through api.transitous.org, whose service terms forbid commercial use.

feeds.name: Germany long-distance rail
feeds.attribution: Timetable data: DELFI e.V. / gtfs.de (CC BY 4.0), © OpenStreetMap contributors
feeds.covers: ICE, IC, EC, ECE, EN (EuroNight), RJ (RailJet) — includes ÖBB, SNCF, SBB, PKP, ČD, MÁV, NS as operating agencies
feeds.notes: Free tier covers the next 30 days. Verified 2026-08-31: 96 routes, 5,354 trips, 1,222 stops, 7 EuroNight routes.

feeds.name: Germany regional rail
feeds.attribution: Timetable data: DELFI e.V. / gtfs.de (CC BY 4.0), © OpenStreetMap contributors
feeds.covers: RB, RE, IRE, S-Bahn and non-federal railways
feeds.notes: ~12MB. Needed so a journey can reach places the long-distance network does not serve.

feeds.name: Spain long-distance rail (Renfe)
feeds.covers: AVE, AVLO, ALVIA, Intercity, AVANT, MD, Regional Exprés
feeds.notes: Rail-only: all 672 routes are route_type=2, so no filtering is needed. Publisher-direct and keyless. Verified 2026-09-01: HTTP 200, 688,573 bytes. Deliberately bypasses the Spanish NAP, which returns 401 without an API key.

feeds.name: Switzerland rail (SBB and partners)
feeds.publisher: Open data platform mobility Switzerland (ODMCH), operated by SBB
feeds.covers: IC, IR, EC, NJ, TGV, ICE, RJX, PE and Swiss regional rail
feeds.notes: 232MB zipped, ~3.7GB unpacked, and there is NO rail-only variant — the file is the whole country including municipal buses, so keepModes filters it during ingest. The permalink 302s to a 60-second presigned S3 URL, so it must be followed each run rather than cached. Switzerland is the hub of European rail: it is where German, French and Italian long-distance services meet. maxRouteType keeps only long-distance and express rail (GTFS extended types 100-105): including Swiss regional and S-Bahn made them 70% of the whole graph and tripled search latency for one small country.

feeds.name: Netherlands rail (NS and partners)
feeds.publisher: OVapi / Stichting OpenGeo, feed produced by Bliksem Labs B.V.
feeds.covers: NS Intercity, Intercity Direct, Sprinter, and international services via NS International
feeds.notes: 213MB zipped and mostly buses, so keepModes filters it during ingest. CC0 imposes no attribution obligation at all; we credit anyway because EU Delegated Regulation 2017/1926 Art. 8(3) requires the source to be shown regardless of licence. Verified 2026-09-01: HTTP 200, 213,222,500 bytes.

feeds.name: France long-distance rail (SNCF Voyageurs)
feeds.attribution: Timetable data: SNCF Voyageurs, via transport.data.gouv.fr (ODbL 1.0)
feeds.covers: TGV, Intercités, TER — 578 rail routes plus 111 SNCF coach routes
feeds.notes: SHARE-ALIKE. ODbL attaches to a derived DATABASE, not only to the file: publishing a database derived from this obliges us to license that derivative under ODbL too. It is fine to serve journey RESULTS, but src/data/network.json must not be published as a dataset while this feed is in it. Verified 2026-09-01: HTTP 200, 4,048,404 bytes.

_deliberatelyExcluded.reason: 272MB of buses, trams and subways. Out of scope for an intercity A→B planner, and it would dominate the graph. Revisit only for first/last-mile.
api.transitous.org prohibits commercial use and requires consuming projects be open source. Their feed CATALOGUE is CC0 and we may use it as a roadmap, but we must never depend on their servers.
DELFI's GTFS-RT realtime feed is CC-BY-SA (share-alike), unlike the CC-BY static feed. Keep it out until it can live in an isolated pipeline stage where share-alike cannot reach the rest of the data.

Italy publishes NeTEx only — a single 370MB trenitalia.xml, no GTFS. Our ingester reads GTFS, so Italy cannot be added without a NeTEx parser. Partial mitigation: the French Trenitalia feed carries Paris–Milano.

Austria's Mobilitätsverbünde host refuses TCP on 443, and every dataset needs a Keycloak OAuth token. Partial mitigation: the German long-distance feed already carries ÖBB as an operating agency with RJ, EN, EC, IC and ICE services into Austria.

The Belgian feed serves 1,489 rail routes but states NO licence at all — unlike its neighbours, which all carry CC-BY-4.0. Technically working, legally unestablished. Do not ingest until a licence is confirmed.
Licence text could not be retrieved. Working feed, unverified terms.
Licence text could not be retrieved, and the download path is undocumented. Working feed, unverified terms.

No defensible licence. Poland publishes NO official rail GTFS: dane.gov.pl carries only urban feeds, and PKP Intercity, PKP PLK and POLREGIO are not registered as data-providing institutions at all. The one official source, pdp-api.plk-sa.pl, is JSON-only behind registration plus 3-5 days of manual approval, and its footer reads "Wszelkie prawa zastrzeżone" (all rights reserved). The CC-BY-4.0 on the gtfs.kasznia.net rehost is the Transitous maintainers own characterisation and traces to no PKP grant, so the rehost may rest on an unfounded licence claim. Excluded on licence grounds, not merely fragility. See docs/research/cz-pl-rail-feeds-2026-09.md

Viable and deferred, not rejected. Czechia has the cleanest licence of any feed examined: the Ministry of Transport publishes via portal.cisjr.cz and data.gov.cz declares CC0 plus explicit disclaimers of copyright, database copyright and sui generis database right. But it ships NeTEx and CZPTT XML only - there is no gtfs folder - so adopting it means owning a NeTEx-to-GTFS converter and synthesising extended route types 100-105 ourselves, since NeTEx has no route_type. Worth doing to remove the single-volunteer dependency; de-risk by diffing converter output against data.jr.ggu.cz before cutting over. Also check the payload: the metadata declares "contains personal data", which CC0 does not waive. See docs/research/cz-pl-rail-feeds-2026-09.md
